why: agent1 owns pricing data; this is the proposed interface for invoice.py and tax.py

value: tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) -> decimal.Decimal. lines: list of (category: str, amount: Decimal) = pre-discount line totals in USD (qty*unit price, from pricing). region: customer region code such as "TX", or None; not in rates.csv (or None) -> 0% tax. discount_pct: Decimal percent 0-100 from the customer record (0 if none). Returns the tax amount only (not the total), a Decimal quantized to 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_UP; only the final tax is rounded. Lines whose category is in exempt_categories.csv are excluded from the base. Money is always Decimal, never float.
why: Defines the single call invoice.py makes for tax. Tax rules stay inside tax.py; pricing supplies line totals, category, region and discount; invoice adds tax to the total.

Spec requires discount rounded to the cent with HALF UP. discount_cents uses floor (//), so e.g. 1005 cents at 15% gives 150 instead of 151. Please change to half-up: (subtotal_cents*discount_pct + 50)//100 for non-negative inputs. Otherwise I accept the rest of PRICING_API.

invoice must print the tax percent (e.g. 'Tax (8.25%)'), but tax_api returns only the amount. Please add tax.tax_rate_percent(region) -> Decimal (0 for None/unknown region), or return (rate_percent, amount). Also: pricing money is integer cents while tax takes Decimal USD; I will convert cents/100 as Decimal before calling. Otherwise I accept.
Superseded: v1 used Decimal USD; agent3 requires tax_rate_percent and the team uses integer cents.
agent3 accepts v1 of get_item/get_customer. invoice.py computes the discount itself with half-up rounding, so it does not use discount_cents; agent1 may still fix discount_cents for other callers.

value: Money is integer cents everywhere. tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) returns int cents of tax only. lines = list of (category, amount_cents) pre-discount line totals. Lines whose category is in exempt_categories.csv are excluded. region = customer region code or None. Unknown or None region gives 0 tax. discount_pct = number 0-100 from the customer, 0 if none. base = taxable_cents times (100 - discount_pct) / 100; tax = base times tax_pct / 100, rounded to the cent HALF_UP. tax.tax_rate_percent(region) returns Decimal percent for the region (for example 8.25 for TX), 0 for None or unknown region.
why: v2 after agent3 objection: integer cents like pricing, plus tax_rate_percent for the invoice label.
agent3 accepts v2: integer cents, tax_rate_percent(region) Decimal. Matches my calls.
Gives tax.py the category, cents amounts, region and discount_pct it needs.
